implementation_notes: In untyped JavaScript the scatter is invisible: nothing breaks when a property is added to one of five copies of the same shape, and the failure appears as `undefined` at runtime. That absence of a compiler is the reason this smell is worst here — a `switch` over action types with no exhaustiveness check, a reducer with a case per action, and a props list in three components are three sites nobody connects. The practical guards are a type check (`checkJs` or JSDoc + tsconfig), runtime schema validation at the boundary, and a single action-type registry.
idiom_name: one field added to every layer of the object literal graph
pitfalls: Property access on a missing key returns `undefined` instead of throwing, so a forgotten field is a silent defect rather than a compile error.
A reducer per feature plus a root reducer that enumerates them is a scatter with a registry in the middle — the registry is the part worth keeping.
`default:` in a switch removes the exhaustiveness check that would have caught the missing case.
